comments.value:
While this would be also a nice feature, I have a work around for now.  I have my own custom sit animation that lowers where I sit to better match the common chair, HOWEVER... it would not be universal, and if chairs have varying heights, it would not work too well.  

That being said, I would like to see this feature, as someone who is often with large avatars, I would like a better function.
Honestly I'm surprised that the current method doesn't use the hipbone as the base location to work from.
@{59715a9e4979f85df8d62ef5|full_name}: The only issue with that is without a custom animation on a larger avi you will sit with your legs in the ground. >_<

@{59715a9e4979f85df8d62ef5|full_name}: I have experimented a bit with this and there are a few more issues. Like how long your avatar's legs are. Basically, without custom animations, a lot of extreme cases break, so until we can find a generic solution that works for everything, you'll need to provide a custom animation if your avatar diverges from "standard". Also, there is the issue that the Chair itself can provide an animation, like if its a chaise-lounge, so the measure points and placement of the avatar need to be completely different.

But if your avatar is too small, your legs will penetrate into the front of the chair (if we place the hip bone at the center of the chair). So the distance from hip to knee must also be measured. Also, avatar's place the "pelvis" bone at very different parts in the rig. This is an extremely complex thing to deal with, and has no simple solution that will look good for everyone.

@{58d60ee5acff4444923bdef0|full_name}: I would hope that linking to the hip bone would alleviate the issues, though yes if your legs are longer they would sink through the ground, but honestly... I would rather have that, then floating off the chair.  it would help keep animations more universal per avatar.  If the chair does its own custom animation, as it is now, you will have that floating, but if based on the hips, there shouldn't be much issue, and having a custom animation on the avatar itself can have the legs up, but if custom on chair, eh... might have some feet sinking, but again... it'd be the lesser of two evils.

@{58d60ee5acff4444923bdef0|full_name}: What if the user has to put in the measured distance in unity? If there, the avatar sits right. If not it looks messed up. But then there are chairs in different sizes, too. So the chair needs has aslo be measured?
@{59715a9e4979f85df8d62ef5|full_name}: the User know as Splink has fixed this issue and has made his prefab publically available, I suggest updating the sdk with this prefab
Closing due to age, please make a new post if it is still relevant.

details:
Right now if you are a bigger or smaller sized avatar you either sink through or hover above the chair you're sitting in.
I propose a change so your hips bone touch the seat of the chair, regardless of avatar size, when you sit down.
title: Let big/small avatars sit properly!
